name: Hanseatic Kontor established at Bergen
summary: German merchants from Lübeck and other Wendish-circle towns secure formal trading privileges at Bergen, establishing the Bryggen Kontor that gives the Hanseatic League a near-monopoly on Norwegian stockfish and grain trade for the next three centuries.

_quarry.structural_significance: Western anchor of the Hanseatic distribution system, paired with Bruges in the Low Countries; demonstrates the League's capacity to extract sovereign-style commercial privileges from northern monarchies.
